candidates.qdq: measured MoE-block output error after quantizing one expert (MXFP4 for 4-bit, int RTN for 3/2)
candidates.router: weight error multiplied by sqrt(routed token count)

decision: Use direct QDQ impact. It won the block-level head-to-head, beat router-weighted error on all six test layers, and produced the best full-depth result at lower byte cost than the router-weighted allocation.
implementation_notes: The 4-bit candidate uses the true W4A16 number format (MXFP4 E2M1, E8M0 scale per 32).
The 3- and 2-bit candidates are int group-32 RTN proxies for IQ3_S and IQ2_S/IQ2_XS; exact IQ QDQ would require the llama.cpp quantizers per tensor.
The own-Coder packer must gain per-expert width support to consume this allocation.

layer_level_comparison.note: QDQ beat router-weighted on every one of the six layers

non_claims: One 512-token calibration sequence; per-layer BF16-input reconstruction.
No end-to-end logits, artifact packing, engine run, or served throughput.
Block-level and layer-level numbers are not comparable to each other; only within each comparison.
question: Which QDQ selection methodology should drive the own-Coder RCO width allocation?
